# R373 v1 — prefill-only native COPY queue selector

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/report study; only this report created. No GPU, model, test, build, import, AST, profiler, service, Git command, or source edit. Main's phase/capture work was left untouched. Fixed measurement worktree remains `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013` at HEAD `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2`; design source read from `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013` at HEAD `54385d6f975a13df5da87f489614d0b729d2aba6`. Source was dirty/concurrent; these are read-time identities, not claim of final tree.

## Decision

A separate, default-OFF prefill selector is technically compatible with the existing `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1` native copy-only route, if it is explicit at stream creation and is scoped only to the ordinary prefill expert-copy stream. Keep the existing global exact `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE=1` gate frozen. Add an independent prefill selector, e.g. exact `STRATA_PREFILL_NATIVE_COPY=1`, whose meaning is “request native COPY only for this explicitly-created prefill stream.” Its default is generic. Do not infer role from an opaque stream, work shape, caller stack, or queue traffic. Do not alter decode graph/verification streams. Existing `copy_stream_create()` is called only in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:705` in this tree, but an explicit creation purpose is still preferable to baking “prefill” into a generic API; callers should name purpose (or use `prefill_copy_stream_create`) and the runtime factory should receive the requested native policy. The native queue remains COPY-only and refuses compute/graph/host_task operations as already enforced in `device.cpp:317-323` and the native wrapper guards.

This is a selection proposal, not a performance/quality adoption claim. The supplied global-on measurements (quiet stock upstreambench.sh --long --runs3; actual 32049, read/reuse 0, out 24; COPY0 prefill median 407.5 ms (403–408), decode 8.6 ms (7.9–9.7); COPY1 prefill 474.8 ms (470.8–478), decode 8.7 ms (8.6–9.3)) show this global-on cohort was slower on prefill and decode effectively overlapped. They do not establish the outcome of a prefill-only selector. They also do not qualify full 256K or correctness. Do not call global-on bench evidence for the proposed implementation.

## Source path and ownership

The existing runtime global selector is `Runtime::create_copy_stream()` at `src/core/device.cpp:326-333`: `copy_engine_requested()` governs all stream creation; service-events forces the generic queue; native path is Level Zero only and native queue creation is already bounded COPY-only. Exact flag parsing is near `device.cpp:197`/the `copy_engine_requested` definition. Runtime streams share the Runtime's SYCL context/device (`include/strata/core/runtime.hpp:23-24, 93-100`). The queue is retained in `EngineStream`; native ownership and queue lifetime are co-located there (`device.cpp:380-405`), and the global COPY flag checks the queue's `copy_only` marker (`device.cpp:309-323`).

Prefill `Impl` owns `m.copy`, created once in init at `prefill.cpp:705-706`, plus event rings and `Stager` (`:711-733`). The dedicated queue carries ordinary expert blob H2D copies from both the sequential layer-major paths (`:2302-2321`, `:2335 onward`; second path `:2594 onward`) and issuer/pipeline path (`:1456 onward`, `:1511-1532`). Copy submissions use `copy_async`/`copy_async_after` and record `m.copied[slot]`; compute waits on those events and copy waits on `m.used`/`m.mgrp_used` before reusing destination slots (`:2350-2366`, corresponding later path around `:2624-2652`). This is explicit prefill work and has identifiable producer/consumer ordering. The ordinary host-to-device token, QSA, PLE uploads are instead commonly submitted on compute stream `m.cs` (`:1380 onward`, `:1360-1374`); host staging of transient or pageable expert weights is performed by `Stager` CPU worker threads (`:245 onward`, `:315-353`) before the queued H2D. A prefill-native selector therefore selects only the existing expert-copy queue; it does not move CPU tasks or all prefill H2D traffic.

At chunk exit/error, existing RAII drains compute and copy queues before stager buffers retire (`:1436-1454`, `:1503-1511`); init/reset/release drains both at `:888` and the `Prefill::run` completion path is separately recorded. Preserve these boundaries. Queue ownership stays in Runtime; `Prefill::Impl` owns the stream handle and destroys it during release/reset only after existing drain. Do not cache a native queue across Runtime/context teardown. Generic fallback must be selected before native import is attempted; once native UR borrowing starts, preserve existing fail-stop/retention contract from `implementation-prefill-native-copy-queue-source-v2.txt` (do not fallback/retry after ambiguous import or insertion failure).

## Minimal change boundary

1. Add an exact, default-OFF prefill selector parsed independently from `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE`; use only at explicit prefill copy-stream creation. Keep the existing global selector and exact semantics untouched.
2. Thread a creation-purpose/policy argument from `Prefill::init` through `gpu::copy_stream_create` to Runtime, so selector cannot affect verifier/decode or unrelated streams. In absence of the prefill selector, preserve generic queue. If native eligibility is unavailable pre-import, use generic queue under existing fallback. Do not add per-copy role guesses or new event loops.
3. Keep all existing event recording/waits, same context/device, source classification and slot reuse. Native path must still be rejected for compute/graph/host-task work. No first-warm special path: first prompt uses same selector and existing queue/event lifetime. On reset/reinit, destroy after drains and recreate under same selector; failed pre-import init can use generic fallback, ambiguous post-import failure remains fail-stop.
4. Preserve the service-event exclusion: current service profiling forces generic (`device.cpp:330-331`), so selector must not bypass it. Preserve fallback if the provider/build does not support Level Zero native import or bounded COPY API group.
5. Phase cache integration: phase-cache VMM is virtual address reservation plus physical mapping (`src/core/phase_cache_backend.cpp:18-40`; actual map/attach code in `src/core/vmm.cpp` and phase-cache owner). Never assume a VMM virtual pointer is a SYCL USM allocation merely because it is device-accessible. The current generic native wrapper uses `sycl::get_pointer_type` for USM classification (`device.cpp:178, 204-208`; `gpu.cpp:235-240` classifies host USM) and copy APIs may have address/USM constraints. Any future phase-cache destination routed to this queue needs an explicit supported-copy contract and source-level/API verification for VMM addresses, plus fallback; do not widen this selector to phase-cache virtual addresses by role inference. The proposed expert-copy destination is existing regular device/USM stage memory, subject to actual path validation.

The key safety condition is producer lifetime: Stager host buffer cannot be reused until its H2D completion credit is returned; destination slot cannot be overwritten until compute's `used` event; compute may consume it only after `copied` event. Keep existing in-order queue behavior and cross-queue event edges intact. Do not add host polling or a second completion system.

## Qualification and adoption gates for Main

No automatic enable until the prefill-only arm has an independently identified selector and is compared against selector-off generic queue with the same workload/configuration. First establish no hidden decode selection and no change in decode graph path; then run repeated independent processes/interleaved arms, report each prefill and decode sample (decode variability requires multiple samples), plus median/range and errors. Use identical model/input/cache residency/warmup/output, full API status and output correctness; separate first-warm from steady samples. Validate default-OFF and exact `=1` parsing, fallback on unsupported/pre-import failure, service-event generic route, native COPY-only refusal, queue/context identity, all event edges, cancellation/error drains, reset/reinit and first-request lifetime. Include VMM-address classification/rejection and generic fallback if any relevant phase cache path is exercised. Keep source/evidence/decision at the work boundary per retention policy. Do not use the global-on prefill slowdown as a quantitative estimate for prefill-only behavior.

R370 v2's safe segmented verifier synchronization finding and R371 v2's decode quantized-roofline reasoning were reviewed as requested. R370 supports that segmented verifier work can already have an explicit completion boundary for CPU route observation; it does not imply the verifier should receive the prefill native queue. R371 is decode compute-path context and provides no evidence for changing decode queue selection.

## Primary references

- SYCL 2020 reference, USM pointer query (`get_pointer_type`; unknown for pointers not recognized as USM): https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/usm_pointer_queries.html
- oneAPI Level Zero interoperability (`make_queue` and queue ownership): https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/backend_interop.html
- Intel oneAPI Level Zero queue/command-list API (native queue and command list distinction): https://oneapi-spec.uxlfoundation.org/specifications/oneapi/v1.3-rev-1/elements/level-zero/source/queue

These references support the general API boundaries; exact availability and semantics remain implementation/backend-specific and must be revalidated for the deployed compiler/runtime.
